direction_summary: Mechanism-aware evaluation with a deterministic executable fixture.

candidates.title: Intervention-sensitive diagnostic
candidates.question: Does the intervention improve the fixed diagnostic score?
candidates.hypothesis: The intervention raises the score by at least 0.1.
candidates.claim: In the toy setting, the intervention improves the fixed diagnostic score.
candidates.why_valuable: It tests a scoped mechanism instead of treating successful execution as evidence.

novelty.uncertainty: The result is intentionally limited to the fixture.

candidates.falsifier: A score below 0.6 under the fixed evaluator.

candidates.title: Evaluator sensitivity boundary
candidates.question: When does the fixed evaluator stop detecting the intervention?
candidates.hypothesis: Small effects fall below the minimum meaningful delta.
candidates.claim: The fixed evaluator has a measurable sensitivity boundary.
candidates.why_valuable: It distinguishes an absent effect from evaluator insensitivity.

novelty.uncertainty: Only a toy evaluator is covered.

candidates.falsifier: Scores remain equally separable at every tested effect size.
candidates.smallest_test: Sweep two effect sizes around the delta.

candidates.title: Negative-result diagnostic value
candidates.question: Can a non-improving run still rule out the named mechanism?
candidates.hypothesis: A valid non-improving metric weakens the scoped mechanism claim.
candidates.claim: A valid negative result updates the mechanism claim without conflating execution failure.
candidates.why_valuable: It makes failed hypotheses useful while preserving execution semantics.

novelty.uncertainty: The workflow behavior needs broader validation.

candidates.falsifier: Negative metrics cannot distinguish the mechanism from a confound.
